title: FMGE PSM Mock 1 - Section 1
subject: Community Medicine
description: FMGE-style 50-question PSM section generated from the reviewed Day 2 PSM source.

questions.stem: The temperature maintained inside an ice-lined refrigerator (ILR) is:
questions.explanation: The ILR, the most important cold-chain equipment at the PHC, keeps vaccines at +2°C to +8°C. −25°C to −15°C is the deep-freezer range.

questions.stem: After a wedding meal, cases of acute gastroenteritis rise sharply and fall within one incubation period. The epidemic type is:
questions.explanation: A single shared exposure produces a sharp rise and fall, with all cases within one incubation period. Repeated exposure would produce successive waves.

questions.stem: Two districts have the same number of maternal deaths and live births, but District Y has twice as many women aged 15–49 years as District X. Which of the following is true?
options: The maternal mortality ratio is lower in District Y
Both the maternal mortality rate and ratio are unchanged
The maternal mortality rate is lower in District Y; the ratio is unchanged
The maternal mortality rate is unchanged; the ratio is lower in District Y
questions.explanation: The maternal mortality rate uses women aged 15–49 as its denominator, and the ratio uses live births. Doubling only the number of women lowers the rate and leaves the ratio unchanged.
questions.answer_label: The maternal mortality rate is lower in District Y; the ratio is unchanged
questions.answer: The maternal mortality rate is lower in District Y; the ratio is unchanged

questions.stem: The Vizag gas leak tragedy was caused by:
questions.explanation: The Vizag tragedy was a styrene gas leak. Methyl isocyanate was the gas in the Bhopal disaster.

questions.stem: Villagers draw water from the same contaminated well over several days, and the epidemic curve shows successive waves. This is:
questions.explanation: Repeated exposure to the same contaminated source produces successive waves of cases. A propagated epidemic spreads from person to person.

questions.stem: As per the Rangarajan Committee, the urban poverty line is a per-capita daily expenditure below:
questions.explanation: The Rangarajan Committee set the poverty line at ₹47 per person per day in urban areas and ₹32 in rural areas.

questions.stem: A male multipurpose worker visits every household once a fortnight to search for fever cases for malaria. This is:
questions.explanation: In active surveillance the health system goes to the community to search for cases, as the malaria MPW does once a fortnight. In passive surveillance, patients report on their own.

questions.stem: In ICD-11, mental, behavioural or neurodevelopmental disorders are classified in:
questions.explanation: ICD-11 places mental, behavioural or neurodevelopmental disorders in Chapter 06. Chapter 21 is a different chapter.

questions.stem: Use of helmets by motorcyclists is an example of:
questions.explanation: Helmet use protects healthy people against a specific injury risk, so it is primary prevention by specific protection.

questions.stem: Reconstituted measles vaccine prepared at 9 AM is given from the same vial at 4 PM. The child is at risk of:
questions.explanation: Reconstituted vaccine must be used within 4 hours. Using the vial 7 hours later risks contamination and toxic shock syndrome, the classic AEFI of reconstituted measles vaccine.

questions.stem: The diluent used to reconstitute BCG vaccine is:
questions.explanation: BCG is reconstituted with normal saline. Distilled water is the diluent for measles, MR and MMR vaccines, and phosphate-buffered saline for JE vaccine.

questions.stem: After a road accident, a man loses his right hand and can no longer write or drive. His inability to write or drive is:
questions.explanation: Losing the hand is the impairment. The resulting inability to write or drive is the disability. Handicap is the loss of the person's expected social role.

questions.stem: The strain used in the live attenuated Japanese encephalitis vaccine is:
questions.explanation: The live attenuated JE vaccine uses the SA-14-14-2 strain. Nakayama is the strain in the killed JE vaccine.

questions.stem: Smallpox was declared globally eradicated on:
questions.explanation: Smallpox was declared globally eradicated on 8 May 1980. March 2014 is when India was certified polio-free.

questions.stem: During an outbreak investigation, the first case to come to the attention of the investigator is the:
questions.explanation: The index case is the first case to come to the investigator's notice. It is not necessarily the primary case, which is the first case in the outbreak.

questions.stem: A single laboratory-confirmed case of wild poliovirus occurs in a region that has been polio-free for years. This is termed:
questions.explanation: An epidemic is occurrence clearly above the normal expectation. Where the expected number is zero, a single wild poliovirus case is an epidemic.

questions.stem: The tablet-based application used by ANMs for RCH data entry is:
questions.explanation: ANMOL (ANM Online) is the tablet-based application ANMs use to enter RCH data.

questions.stem: Detention of the healthy contacts of a case until the maximum incubation period has passed is called:
questions.explanation: Quarantine restricts healthy contacts for up to the maximum incubation period. Isolation separates cases until recovery.

questions.stem: The intranasal COVID-19 vaccine developed in India is:
questions.explanation: iNCOVACC is the indigenous COVID-19 vaccine given as intranasal drops. Covaxin, from the same Indian manufacturer, is an intramuscular injection.

questions.stem: In an outbreak, 10 of 250 cases die. The case fatality rate is:
questions.explanation: Case fatality rate = deaths ÷ cases × 100 = 10 ÷ 250 × 100 = 4%.

questions.stem: The dose of human rabies immunoglobulin is:
questions.explanation: Human rabies immunoglobulin is given at 20 IU/kg; equine RIG at 40 IU/kg. It is infiltrated around the wound.

questions.stem: A veterinarian who completed rabies pre-exposure vaccination is bitten by a rabid dog. After wound washing, he should receive:
options: Two IM doses on days 0 and 3
Five IM doses on days 0, 3, 7, 14 and 28
Rabies immunoglobulin plus five IM doses
questions.explanation: After wound washing, a previously vaccinated person needs only two IM booster doses, on days 0 and 3.
questions.answer_label: Two IM doses on days 0 and 3
questions.answer: Two IM doses on days 0 and 3

questions.stem: A vial within its expiry date carries the vaccine vial monitor shown. The correct action is:
options: Do a shake test before deciding
Return the vial to the district store
questions.image_alt: Vaccine vial monitor: a square inside a circle
questions.image_source: p.74 | second VVM stage (Gr 2), cropped without its label or tick
questions.explanation: The VVM shows cumulative heat exposure. While the inner square is lighter than the outer circle (stages 1 and 2), the vaccine can be used. Once the square matches or is darker than the circle (stages 3 and 4), the vial is discarded.

questions.stem: The interval between the onset of symptoms in the primary case and in the secondary case is called:
questions.explanation: The serial interval is the gap between symptom onset in the primary case and in the secondary case. Generation time runs from receipt of infection to maximal infectivity.

questions.stem: A vaccine carrier holds approximately:
questions.explanation: A vaccine carrier holds about 16–20 vials and keeps them cold for 12–24 hours.

questions.stem: A man is bitten on the leg by a stray dog, and the wound is bleeding. The first step in managing the wound is:
options: Infiltrate rabies immunoglobulin around the wound
Wash with soap and water for 15–20 minutes
questions.explanation: Wound care starts with thorough washing with soap and water for 15–20 minutes. RIG infiltration and antibiotics follow, and suturing is contraindicated.
questions.answer_label: Wash with soap and water for 15–20 minutes
questions.answer: Wash with soap and water for 15–20 minutes

questions.stem: The Reproductive and Child Health (RCH) programme was launched in:
questions.explanation: The RCH programme began in 1997, after the Child Survival and Safe Motherhood programme of 1992.

questions.stem: All of the following are BEmONC signal functions EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: The seven BEmONC functions include manual removal of placenta, oxytocics, antibiotics, anticonvulsants, assisted delivery, vacuum aspiration and newborn resuscitation. Blood transfusion and surgery are added only at CEmONC.

questions.stem: A district has 8 prevalent leprosy cases per 1,00,000 population. This indicates that:
options: The elimination level has not been reached
The elimination level has been reached
Leprosy has been eradicated in the district
Prevalence cannot be judged without incidence data
questions.explanation: 8 per 1,00,000 equals 0.8 per 10,000, which is below the leprosy elimination level of less than 1 per 10,000.
questions.answer_label: The elimination level has been reached
questions.answer: The elimination level has been reached

questions.stem: The Anemia Mukt Bharat IFA tablet shown contains:
questions.image_alt: Blister strip of round red tablets
questions.image_source: p.107 | tablet photograph (right), cropped without the composition text
questions.explanation: The red Anemia Mukt Bharat IFA tablet contains 60 mg elemental iron and 500 µg (0.5 mg) folic acid. 5 mg is ten times the folic acid content.

questions.stem: After a home delivery, the ASHA makes postnatal home visits on days:
questions.explanation: After a home delivery the ASHA makes seven visits, starting on day 1. After an institutional delivery the visits start on day 3, six in all.

questions.stem: The only vaccine contraindicated during lactation is:
questions.explanation: Lactation is a contraindication only for yellow fever vaccine. The other live vaccines listed are not contraindicated during breastfeeding.

questions.stem: The correct method of preparing an ice pack is to:
options: Add salt to the water before freezing
Fill it with warm water just before use
Fill it to the marked water level, with nothing added
questions.explanation: An ice pack is filled with plain water up to the marked level. Nothing, including salt, is added to the water.
questions.answer_label: Fill it to the marked water level, with nothing added
questions.answer: Fill it to the marked water level, with nothing added

questions.stem: In RMNCH+A, "+A" stands for:
questions.explanation: RMNCH+A stands for Reproductive, Maternal, Newborn and Child health plus Adolescent health, the strategy used in the RCH programme.

questions.stem: Which of the following vaccines is contraindicated in pregnancy?
questions.explanation: Qdenga is a live attenuated tetravalent dengue vaccine, and live vaccines are contraindicated in pregnancy. Td, IPV and Covaxin are not live vaccines.

questions.stem: As per its licensed schedule, Cervavac for a 13-year-old girl is given as:
questions.explanation: Cervavac, the Indian quadrivalent HPV vaccine, is licensed as two doses at 0 and 6 months for 9–14 years and three doses for 15–26 years. WHO SAGE allows one or two doses, but the product's own schedule is two.

questions.stem: Brachial neuritis is an adverse event following immunization with:
questions.explanation: Brachial neuritis is linked to tetanus toxoid (TT/Td). Rotavirus vaccine is linked to intussusception, and MMR to thrombocytopenia.

questions.stem: Covaxin is a:
questions.explanation: Covaxin is a killed whole-virion vaccine, given as two 0.5 mL IM doses 4–6 weeks apart. Covishield is the viral-vector vaccine.

questions.stem: An unvaccinated 14-month-old had household contact with a measles case 2 days ago. The best management is to:
options: Observe, and vaccinate only if no rash develops in 14 days
Avoid vaccination, as it is contraindicated after exposure
Vaccinate after the incubation period is over
questions.explanation: Measles vaccine given within 3 days of exposure can still protect. At 48 hours this child is within that window.

questions.stem: An 18-month-old child attends for routine immunization under the UIP. The vaccines due are:
options: MR2 + DPT booster-1 + OPV booster + JE2
BCG + OPV-0 + hepatitis B birth dose
DPT-2 + OPV-2 + hepatitis B-2 + Hib-2 + RVV-2
MR1 + JE1 + vitamin A first dose
questions.explanation: At 16–24 months the UIP gives MR2, DPT booster-1, OPV booster and JE2. MR1 and JE1 are given at 9–12 months.
questions.answer_label: MR2 + DPT booster-1 + OPV booster + JE2
questions.answer: MR2 + DPT booster-1 + OPV booster + JE2

questions.stem: An 18-month-old child is due for vitamin A prophylaxis under the UIP. The volume of the standard vitamin A solution given is:
questions.explanation: From 16–18 months the dose is 2 lakh IU. The standard solution contains 1 lakh IU/mL, so 2 mL is given.

questions.stem: A district records 12 maternal deaths and 30,000 live births in a year. The maternal mortality ratio is:
questions.explanation: Maternal mortality ratio = maternal deaths ÷ live births × 100,000 = 12 ÷ 30,000 × 100,000 = 40.

questions.stem: Cold-chain equipment at the district (CHC) level is:
questions.explanation: District and CHC stores use large ILRs and large deep freezers, holding about one month's stock. Walk-in coolers and freezers are used at state and regional stores.

questions.stem: The minimum number of antenatal visits recommended under the RCH programme is:
questions.explanation: The RCH programme's minimum is 4 antenatal visits; WHO recommends a minimum of 8 contacts.

questions.stem: The lowest level at which vaccines are stored in the cold chain is the:
questions.explanation: The PHC, with its ILR and deep freezer, is the lowest level where vaccines are stored. Sub-centres do not store vaccines; they receive them in vaccine carriers for each session.

questions.stem: The hidden (submerged) part of the disease iceberg is detected by:
questions.explanation: The submerged part of the iceberg (carriers, subclinical and asymptomatic cases) is found by screening, the epidemiologist's task. The visible tip of clinical cases is found by diagnosis.

questions.stem: The best indicator of combined maternal and newborn care is:
questions.explanation: The perinatal mortality rate is the best indicator of combined maternal and newborn care. The maternal mortality ratio indicates maternal care alone.

questions.stem: A newborn is due for BCG and hepatitis B vaccine. The correct plan is:
options: BCG 0.5 mL IM in the right arm; hepatitis B 0.05 mL intradermal in the thigh
BCG 0.05 mL subcutaneous in the right arm; hepatitis B 0.5 mL intradermal in the left deltoid
BCG 0.05 mL intradermal over the left deltoid; hepatitis B 0.5 mL IM in the anterolateral thigh
BCG 0.5 mL intradermal in the thigh; hepatitis B 0.05 mL subcutaneous in the right arm
questions.source: PDF pp.53, 70 | E2 | Schedule + route table
questions.explanation: Both vaccines are due at birth. Newborn BCG is 0.05 mL intradermal over the left deltoid, and hepatitis B is 0.5 mL IM in the anterolateral thigh.
questions.answer_label: BCG 0.05 mL intradermal over the left deltoid; hepatitis B 0.5 mL IM in the anterolateral thigh
questions.answer: BCG 0.05 mL intradermal over the left deltoid; hepatitis B 0.5 mL IM in the anterolateral thigh

questions.stem: The switch from trivalent to bivalent OPV in 2016 removed poliovirus type 2 because:
options: Wild poliovirus type 2 had been eradicated
Type 2 antigen was unstable in the cold chain
Type 2 caused most cases of vaccine-associated paralysis
questions.explanation: Wild poliovirus type 2 was eradicated in 2015, so the April 2016 global switch removed type 2 from OPV and replaced tOPV (P1, P2, P3) with bOPV (P1, P3).
questions.answer_label: Wild poliovirus type 2 had been eradicated
questions.answer: Wild poliovirus type 2 had been eradicated

questions.stem: Rehabilitation belongs to which level of prevention?
questions.explanation: Tertiary prevention covers disability limitation and rehabilitation. Secondary prevention is early diagnosis and treatment.
